item.title: Gifu Events 2026: Takayama Festival, Gujo Odori & Cormorant Fishing
item.description: Gifu’s mountainous heart hosts some of Japan’s most refined and enduring traditions. The Takayama Festival’s ornate automaton floats are counted among the country’s most beautiful; Gujo Odori is a dance the whole town joins for two months, culminating in four all-night sessions; and on the Nagara River, cormorant fishing has continued unbroken for 1,300 years. Add the winter magic of Shirakawa-go’s illuminated thatched village, and Gifu rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Takayama Spring & Autumn Festivals: Among Japan's Most Beautiful — Guide
item.description: The Takayama Festivals are held twice a year, the Sanno Matsuri in April (spring) and the Hachiman Matsuri in October (autumn), and are counted among Japan’s three most beautiful festivals. Both feature parades of the town’s spectacular yatai floats, masterpieces of Hida carpentry decorated with gilding and carvings, alongside mechanical marionette (karakuri) performances that draw gasps from the crowds. The evening processions, when the illuminated floats are pulled through the old town by lantern light, are a particular highlight of these centuries-old celebrations.
